# camenc zero-copy: verified on the board (2026-10-05)

## What the arrangement is

The encoder is given the buffer the capture driver demosaiced into, instead of
the application copying the frame into a buffer of the encoder's.

Three pieces, all in `contest2026_062_PharosTech`:

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `chips/rk3576/rk3576_vicap.c` | `.alloc`/`.free` hooks on the imgdata ops, so the capture frame heap comes from the DMA heap — the one heap on the part that is identity-mapped, hence the only one whose addresses are physical |
| `chips/rk3576/vepu/rk3576_vepu_codec.c` | `vepu_buffer_is_ours` → `vepu_buffer_usable` + `vepu_buffer_reachable`: the test became the hardware's own requirement (64-byte aligned at both ends, wholly below 4 GiB) rather than "did this driver allocate it". Output side accepts `USERPTR` |
| `app/camenc/camenc_main.c` | `g_zerocopy` decides once per stream; `camenc_setup_import` asks for containers without backing store, `camenc_queue_import` names the camera buffer's address per frame |

The reasoning that made this possible: the encoder's MMU is in pass-through, so
the addresses in its registers have to be physical. Asking "is this my
allocation" refused the camera's buffer by construction, and that was the only
thing standing in the way.

## Verified, and how

Temporarily added a `-z` switch meaning *refuse to run unless the frames are
encoded where they lie*: the two places that used to fall back to copying became
hard errors naming which precondition failed, and the copy branch became
unreachable.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| default mode (3 = 1280x720@30) | stream played, picture correct |
| `-m 1` (1296x960@30) | stream played, picture correct |
| `-m 0` (1920x1080) | **refused** — encoder pads to 1088 rows, camera gives 1080 |
| `-m 1 -W 1280` (crop) | **refused** — widths disagree |

The negatives are what make the positives mean anything: a flag that was not
wired up would have shown the same "it plays" as a flag that was.

`-z` was then removed, as agreed. The source is back to the fallback, and the
firmware was rebuilt so no trace of the switch remains in either.

## The technique, for reuse

This is the pattern to reach for when two code paths produce the same observable
result and only a counter tells them apart:

1. Make the path you do not want **unreachable**, rather than merely unlikely.
2. Turn its precondition into a hard refusal that names what failed.
3. Run the cases that must refuse. If they do not, the switch is not wired and
   the positive run proved nothing.

It works without a serial console, which matters here — see `AGENTS.md`.

## Open

- **The performance result was never captured.** The verification was structural,
  not quantitative: `copy 0/0`, `sum` against `period`, and the frame rate were
  not read. So it is *not* yet known whether the reclaimed copy (measured at
  5.8 ms/frame) brought the single core from ~27.4 fps to the 31.25 fps the
  camera offers. The arithmetic says it should (34.9 − 5.8 = 29.1 ms < 32 ms),
  and that arithmetic is the only basis so far.
- **1920x1080 still copies**, by design. Making it zero-copy would need the
  capture driver to write the chroma plane at `v_stride` rows rather than at the
  picture height — see the magenta-band note in `board-and-build.md`.
- The camenc-side guard mirrors the driver's rule but is missing the
  `size % 64` half of it. All four modes' input sizes happen to be 64-aligned, so
  it is latent rather than live. Worth closing when the area is next touched.

# camenc thread-model refactor: state and plan

## The route, and why

camenc is the contest sample delivery. It will run SMP eventually, but **not
yet**: SMP is cheap to switch on and would dull the incentive to optimise, and
the compute-heavy part (the NEON demosaic) is already at its limit — making that
faster means redesigning it for several cores, not turning SMP on.

So the order is: **get the concurrency right first, then look at SMP.**

## The constraint that shapes everything

Single core (`CONFIG_NCPUS=1`). Measured on 1296x960: the VICAP worker needs
22.9 ms/frame, camenc's non-waiting work 12 ms — 34.9 ms against a 32 ms frame
period, hence ~27.4 fps.

**Threading does not reduce that total.** Splitting work across threads on one
core buys structure and deadline protection, not throughput. Getting the frame
rate back needs *less work*, which is what zero-copy (5.8 ms) and reading the raw
frame where it lies (7.8 ms) were for.

## Scheduler facts (checked, not assumed)

| | Value | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| camenc | priority **100** | `CONFIG_EXAMPLES_CAMENC_PRIORITY` |
| VICAP worker | priority **100** | `CONFIG_SCHED_LPWORKPRIORITY`; queued on `LPWORK` in `rk3576_vicap.c` |
| HPWORK | 192 | system, unrelated to the camera |
| cores | 1 | `CONFIG_NCPUS` |
| round-robin slice | 200 ms | `CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL`; effectively "yield at blocking points" |

★ The plan carried over from the earlier memory said "raise the thread above
LPWORK because LPWORK is currently the lowest priority". That is **not** the
situation: LPWORK sits at 100, the same as camenc. The two are peers today.

Also: **do not raise LPWORK.** It is shared by every driver in the system. Give
the encode thread a higher number instead, and put the network thread below.

| Thread | Proposed |
| --- | --- |
| encode + mux + AE | 110 |
| VICAP worker (LPWORK) | 100 — unchanged |
| network | 90 |
| control | 90, event-driven |

The encode thread spends most of its time blocked inside the encoder's `QBUF`,
so priority 110 does not squeeze the VICAP worker's 22.9 ms; it preempts only
for the ~4 ms of mux, emit and 3A, which is exactly the deadline protection
wanted.

## The four threads

| Thread | Job |
| --- | --- |
| 1 VICAP worker | already exists (kernel LPWORK): demosaic + 3A measurement, writes VEPU-geometry NV12 into the DMA-heap pool, cleans cache |
| 2 encode + mux + AE | dequeue camera frame → hand to encoder (blocks until the VEPU ISR) → dequeue bitstream → mux → emit; run the AE/AWB decision each frame, which is a natural per-frame beat |
| 3 network | non-blocking accept/recv/send plus HTTP, fed from a **bounded** segment queue, dropping oldest |
| 4 control | policy only; starts 2 and 3; mode changes go quiesce → reconfigure → resume |

## Where the code stands

The main loop is `for (; i < frames; i++)` in `camenc_main.c`, and one pass is:

```
mode-change check → DQBUF camera → [copy] → QBUF encoder (blocks ~24 ms)
→ DQBUF encoder → mux → emit (file + WS publish) → 3A → QBUF camera back
→ every 100 frames, report → camenc_ws_poll (non-blocking, at frame end)
```

Stages are accounted as `camera copy encode drain mux file clients serve`.

| Step | State |
| --- | --- |
| 1 pool into the DMA heap, VEPU geometry | done |
| 2 ownership of `vepu_check_buf` | done |
| 3 camenc wired to it (zero-copy) | done, **verified on the board** — see `camenc-zerocopy.md` |
| 4 split thread 2; pool state machine | not started |
| 5 split thread 3 + bounded segment queue | not started |
| 6 thread 4 control; mode switch quiesce/resume | not started |

### Notes that will save time on step 4

- The "pool state machine" is mostly already V4L2: `DQBUF` means held, `QBUF`
  means returned. Of the intended `free → filled → encoding → free`, the
  `encoding` state is just "camenc is holding it". What genuinely has to be added
  is drop counting and the rule that a missing free slot drops a frame instead of
  blocking. Do not invent an abstraction the driver already provides.
- `camenc_ws.c` is already shaped as a non-blocking event loop, so step 5 is
  mostly about *where* `camenc_ws_poll` is called from, plus turning
  `camenc_ws_publish` into a push onto the bounded queue.
- `camenc_ui_command` already only records intent (it runs inside the poll
  callback); the loop acts on it at the top of a frame. That shape survives the
  split as-is.
- A mode change must go through the existing `rk3576_vicap_reconfigure` and
  `rk3576_csi_host_set_lane_rate`. The uninit/init path **hung the board and
  tripped the watchdog** the one time it was exercised.

### Honest expectation for step 4

On one core the split should be worth roughly **0 fps**. It is structure,
deadline protection and SMP readiness. If the frame rate is the goal, the
work-reduction steps are the ones that matter.

`~/.cache/ccache`.

Firmware is flashed by hand on another machine. N-Boot A/B: the new `nuttx.bin`
replaces `nuttx_a.img`; SD-card boot is the alternative.

## Traps that have already cost time

- **`defconfig` edits are not re-expanded into `.config`.** CMake regenerates it
  only when the file is missing or its *path* changes, not its contents. An
  incremental build then silently uses the old value. Fix: `rm -rf
  cmake_out/<cfg>` and rebuild, then confirm the option in
  `cmake_out/<cfg>/include/nuttx/config.h`. This trap disguises itself as "my
  code change broke it".
- **Editing `web/page.html` does not rebuild the firmware.** It reaches the
  binary through `.incbin`, which the dependency scan cannot see, so the board
  keeps serving the old page and it looks like browser caching. Check with
  `grep -ao "<a string from the new page>" cmake_out/<cfg>/nuttx`.
- **A stale binary looks like a stale source.** Before flashing, compare
  `nuttx.bin`'s mtime against every source, or just run ninja and confirm it has
  nothing to do.

## The encoder's frame geometry, and the magenta band

The encoder reads a source buffer as luma over `y_stride × v_stride` with the
chroma plane at **`y_stride × v_stride`** — the *allocated* height, not the
picture height. `v_stride = align(height, 16)`.

This bit 1920x1080: the picture is 1080 rows, `v_stride` is 1088, so the chroma
plane belongs at `1920×1088 = 2088960`. Code that used `height × stride`
(`2073600`) put it 8 rows early, leaving the bottom 8 chroma rows never written —
which a decoder shows as a **magenta band across the bottom 16 lines**, reading
whatever the memory last held. Every other mode has `align(h,16) == h`, so the
two agree and the bug stayed hidden.

**`src_size`/`dst_size` are allocation sizes, not picture sizes.** Anything that
fills NV12 as `w*h*3/2` will break on a height that is not a multiple of 16.

The capture driver writes exactly the picture geometry — luma stride `width`,
chroma at `width × height` — so for 16-multiple heights the two devices already
agree, which is what makes zero-copy possible at all.

## Cache

The VEPU DMA **does not snoop**. The contract is explicit maintenance, and both
sides already do it: VICAP cleans the demosaiced frame after the demosaic, VEPU
cleans the source before a job and invalidates the destination after. The DMA
heap is normal, cacheable, identity-mapped memory with 64-byte lines, so a buffer
must be 64-byte aligned at both ends, or the maintenance touches its neighbours.

## Streaming

- The WebSocket carries fragmented MP4, one fragment per frame.
- **Dropping a fragment breaks every following P picture**, and a decoder shows
  that as a frame of garbage rather than one missing frame. The recovery is to
  mark the client `waiting` and skip until the next key fragment; the encoder's
  key/P flags make that work.
- `CAMENC_WS_MAX_SEGMENT` is 512 KiB.
- camenc asks the encoder for groups of **15** pictures (`CAMENC_DEFAULT_GOP`);
  the driver's own default is 2 (`RK3576_VEPU_DEFAULT_GOP`). Measured on a drawn
  source: groups of 4 are 51% of the rate of groups of 2.
- The encoder has **no rate control** — it runs at a fixed QP, so the only lever
  on bitrate is the quantiser.

`chips/rk3576/vepu/rk3576_vepu_codec.c`.

**我建议 AE 留在线程2**：AE 本质是**伺服环**（每帧采样→计算→施加），不是策略。策略是 auto/manual、目标亮度、手动值、预设——归线程4。线程4 → 线程2 单向传设定值（mailbox + 版本号足够），线程2 每帧读快照。这样"策略"和"伺服"分开，但不会分裂设备所有权。


**外设不要走 uninit/init。** 那条路实测挂死并触发 WDT。走已有的 `rk3576_vicap_reconfigure` + `rk3576_csi_host_set_lane_rate`。

   - 网络 = listen fd + 客户端 fd
   - 定时 = poll 的 timeout

I should give an honest assessment of the design idea.

**这个方向是对的，而且我认为它比四线程更适合当前阶段。** 理由（前面几轮已经论证过的）：
- 单核上线程化不减总 CPU，四线程的收益只有"编码等待的 24ms 里服务网络"和 deadline 隔离。

查清了，可以给你确定的答案。

## 直接回答：多个 semaphore 等任一——**没有这个原语**

POSIX 的 `sem_wait()`/`sem_timedwait()` 只能等一个，NuttX 没有扩展它。**但你不需要它——因为你这个设计里每一个唤醒源本来就是 fd，而 `poll()` 就是"多路任一即唤醒"。** 我把每个源都验证了一遍：

| 唤醒源 | 证据 |
|---|---|
| 相机帧就绪 | `capture_poll` 在 fops 里（`v4l2_cap.c:359`），帧完成时 `poll_notify(..., POLLIN)`（`:2024`） |
| 编码器出帧 | `g_codec_fops` 注册了 `codec_poll`（`v4l2_m2m.c:218`），且 **QBUF 里就 notify**（`:1175`） |
| 新客户端连接 | `tcp_listen.c:297` 发 `TCP_BACKLOG` → `tcp_netpoll.c:86` 映射成 `POLLIN` |
| 客户端收发 | 各 client fd |
| 定时/状态行 | `poll()` 的 timeout 参数 |

`CONFIG_POLL=1` 也是开的。

★ 第三行正是我上一轮标"未验证"的那条——**现在是好消息**。当时我担心 NuttX 的 poll 不会因 backlog 里的连接唤醒，查了 `tcp_listen.c` 和 `tcp_netpoll.c`，它会。

所以：**`poll(fds, n, timeout)` 一次调用，语义就是你想要的"任意一个触发就唤醒"**，内建、无锁、无线程。

## 顺带：如果你真的想要"位掩码式事件组"，NuttX 有

`nxevent` 的语义**恰好是 any/all**（`event_wait.c:76`）：

```c
waitany = !(eflags & NXEVENT_WAIT_ALL);
if (waitany && (events & event->events))                    /* 任一位置位 → 返回 */
else if (!waitany && (event->events & events) == events)    /* 全置位 → 返回 */
```

而且 `nxevent_post()` 文档明写 "may be called from an interrupt handler"。**但 camenc 现在用不上**：`nxevent_wait/post` 是内核内部接口（文档："should not be used by applications"），用户态入口是 Named Events（`CONFIG_FS_NAMED_EVENTS`，`/var/event`），而**本 build 没开**。

结论：**别用 semaphore，用 `poll()`。** 将来真出现非 fd 的唤醒源（ISR 或别的线程），用 **self-pipe** 把它变成 fd 塞进 poll 集合即可——NuttX 没有 eventfd（我查了，`CONFIG_EVENT_FD` 不存在），pipe 就行。

## 对你这个"单线程非阻塞状态机"想法的评估

**方向是对的，而且我认为它比四线程更适合现阶段。** 前几轮已经论证过：单核上线程化不减总 CPU，四线程的收益只有两点——(1) 编码等待的 24ms 里服务网络，(2) deadline 隔离。而 (2) 其实**不来自线程**，来自 `camenc_ws` 的非阻塞发送 + 有界缓冲 + 丢帧重同步，单线程一样有。单线程还省掉了优先级调优、线程间 mailbox、quiesce 握手的一大半。

**但有一件事必须先说清，否则你会失望：按现在的驱动，状态机每帧只会回到 `poll()` 一次。**

因为整帧是一条阻塞直线：

```
DQBUF 相机 → QBUF 编码器（★ ioctl 内部同步等 VEPU ~24ms）→ DQBUF 输出 → mux → emit
```

我确认了 `vepu_service()` 被 5 个 ioctl 处理函数直接调用（`rk3576_vepu_codec.c:1271/1279/1317/1324/1544`），job 是在 ioctl 里同步跑完的。所以"非阻塞状态机"里 **ENCODING 这个状态是阻塞的**，循环在这一帧回不到 poll——**这跟今天的循环行为完全一样**。

所以第一版状态机拿到的是**结构收益**（唤醒源统一、状态显式、好改），**不是行为收益**。这一点要事先认清。

## 真正的收益在第二步：把 QBUF 改成"投递即返回"

那时编码完成会通过编码器 fd 的 POLLIN 通知循环（`v4l2_m2m.c:1175` 已经在 QBUF 路径里 notify 了），循环就能在原来那 24ms 里回去服务网络。

**而这正是四线程模型想拿到的东西，却一个线程都不需要。**

而且这一步比之前估计的小得多：poll 的管线已经有了，改的是驱动的 QBUF 路径（别在里面同步跑 job）+ ISR 完成 job 后填 capture buffer。计划里那句"暂不做"要改成"**等第一步把循环掰成状态机之后再做**"——那才是它变便宜的时机。

## 建议顺序

| 步 | 内容 | 行为变化 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 相机缓冲提前归还（上一轮 ★1） | 是（帧率），独立可验 |
| 2 | 主循环改成 `poll` + 显式状态机，**QBUF 仍阻塞** | **无**——帧率/画面/`us/frame` 应与现在一致，正好当回归判据 |
| 3 | async QBUF，ENCODING 变事件驱动 | 是，需要重新测量 |
| 4 | SMP / 多线程 | 推迟到有证据说单线程不够 |

## 状态机草图

```
WAIT       poll({camfd, listen_fd, client fds}, timeout)   ← 唯一的休眠点
           ↑ 返回后先处理 socket 事件（accept/recv/send），这就是"服务网络"
FRAME      DQBUF 相机；判定零拷贝
ENCODING   [可选拷贝] → QBUF 编码器 → DQBUF 输出      ★ 今天这里阻塞 ~24ms
MUXING     camenc_stream_write → emit（文件 + WS publish）
RETURNING  QBUF 编码器输出、QBUF 相机                  ← 提前到这里
           → 回 WAIT
旁路        QUIESCE → RECONFIGURE → RESUME（模式切换）
```

跟今天相比唯一的实质差别是：**网络服务从"每帧末尾无条件调一次"变成"poll 说谁就绪才处理谁"**，其余结构等价——这正是你想要的"平时休眠、被唤醒才推进"。

| 项 | 值（640x480@60） |

| mux 总计（含写入文件） | **277µs**，峰值 525µs |
| 其中纯装箱（建 fMP4 box） | ≈ **120µs**（277 − file 160） |

## 2. 为它单开线程吃 SMP 红利？

**为 mux 开线程不值**——它才 0.12ms 的 CPU。

但你的直觉指向了一个真问题，而且方向是对的：**emit 路径（mux + 文件 + fan-out）是唯一有实打实 SMP 红利的地方**，理由是：

- demosaic 15ms 是最大的一块 CPU，但它在**内核 worker** 里，要拆多核得重新设计（你早就说过）
- encode 24ms 是**硬件**在跑，不占 CPU

它在单核上也有收益，但不是吞吐而是**鲁棒性**：主循环本来就有阻塞窗口（1296x960 的 encode 24ms、640x480 的 DQBUF 12.75ms），sink 线程可以在那些窗口里跑，把磁盘延迟**吸收掉**而不是延长帧周期。

**建议：现在不开，但把 emit 的边界做成"入队"**（有界 + 丢 oldest + 计数）。这样将来加 sink 线程是局部改动。跟事件循环是同一条逻辑——先把形状摆对，优化等证据。

## 3. 编码等待期间客户端连进来——这题你有一半前提是错的

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 640x480@60 | ≈3.2ms（15.98 − 12.75 等待） | 3.77ms | 7 / 16ms | **是，约 56% 空闲** |
| 1296x960@30 | 12ms | 22.9ms | 34.9 / 32ms | **否，超订** |

### 层二：最坏延迟其实没想象中糟

- **TCP 握手不受影响**：`CONFIG_NET_TCPBACKLOG=8`，协议栈自己完成三次握手并排队，客户端不会被挂着。

### 层三：要更快，有两条路，一条免费

**(a) 免费的：把"等相机"也变成 poll 点。**

## `accept()` 你永远不会等它

顺序是反过来的：

```c
poll({listen_fd, camfd, 编码器fd, 各 client fd}, timeout)   ← 只在这里睡
```

因为连接**已经在 backlog 里了**。`nuttx/net/tcp/tcp_accept.c:223-232`：

```c
/* Check the backlog to see if there is a connection already pending for
 * ... */
state.acpt_newconn = tcp_backlogremove(conn);
```

所以"等待 accept 的时候等不了别的"这个情形**不会出现**——你不在 accept 里等，你在 poll 里等，而 poll 等的是**整个集合**。

## "客户端永远不连接，主循环会永远等着吗？"

不会。poll 等的是那一堆 fd 的**任意一个**，而相机一秒送 30~60 帧——**poll 每帧都会醒**，跟有没有客户端毫无关系。就算理论上真的什么都没有，timeout 也会兜住。

**这就是 poll 和阻塞 accept 的本质区别**：阻塞 accept 只等一件事，其它事件来了也不会醒；poll 同时等所有事，谁先来醒谁。

## "等到超时也挺浪费时间的吧？"——这里是最关键的一处纠正

**超时的等待是 0 CPU 的，不是自旋。** `nuttx/fs/vfs/fs_poll.c:495`：

```c
ret = nxsem_tickwait(sem, MSEC2TICK((clock_t)timeout));
```

`nxsem_tickwait` 是**带期限的信号量睡眠**——线程被调度器挂起，直到"有人 post 这个信号量"或"tick 期限到"。这期间它一次都不会被调度，**不消耗任何 CPU**。

所以 timeout 的性质是**兜底安全网**，不是轮询周期：

- 设成 200ms ⇒ 最坏情况下每 5 秒 25 次空唤醒，代价可以忽略
- 而且我们这里根本用不到它兜底，相机本身就把我们叫醒了 30~60 次/秒
- 真想省，设 `-1`（无限等）也行；留个 timeout 只是为了周期性杂活（比如状态行）

```c
for (;;)
  {
    n = poll(fds, nfds, 200);            /* 唯一的睡眠点：0 CPU，任一事件唤醒 */

    if (listen 就绪)   while (accept() >= 0) ;   /* backlog 取，不阻塞；循环排空 */
    if (client 就绪)   recv / send（非阻塞）

    if (编码器 就绪)   DQBUF 输出 → mux → emit   ← 第 2 步之后才有这一支
    if (超时)          周期性杂活
  }
```

listen fd 照旧设 `O_NONBLOCK` 作双保险，这样即使 backlog 里那条被别处取走了，accept 也只会返回 EAGAIN 而不是挂住。

# camenc: conversion to a non-blocking event loop — construction plan

Status: **planned, not started** (2026-10-05). Supersedes the four-thread model in
`camenc-refactor-state.md`; that file's scheduler analysis still stands, but the
threading is now off the table in favour of one non-blocking loop.

## The decision

One thread, one `poll()`, an explicit state machine. Threading was dropped
because on a single core it reduces no work — it only moves it — while costing
priority tuning, mailboxes and quiesce handshakes that a loop does not need.

The wake primitive is `poll()`, **not** semaphores. There is no "wait on N
semaphores, wake on any" in POSIX, and none is needed: every wake source here is
already a file descriptor, and `poll()` is exactly that primitive. Verified:

| Fact | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| A completed capture frame wakes poll | `capture_poll` in the fops (`v4l2_cap.c:359`); `poll_notify(..., POLLIN)` on completion (`:2024`) |
| A queued encoder capture buffer wakes poll | `codec_poll` in `g_codec_fops` (`v4l2_m2m.c:218`); `poll_notify` in the qbuf path (`:1175`) |
| A new connection wakes poll | `tcp_listen.c:297` posts `TCP_BACKLOG` → `tcp_netpoll.c:86` maps it to `POLLIN` |
| DQBUF can be non-blocking | `v4l2_cap.c:2406-2408`: with `O_NONBLOCK` and nothing ready it returns `-EAGAIN` |
| `accept()` will not block after poll says readable | the connection is already in the backlog: `tcp_accept.c:223-232` |
| A `poll()` timeout costs no CPU | `fs_poll.c:495` — `nxsem_tickwait(sem, MSEC2TICK(timeout))`, a plain semaphore sleep |

⚠ A timeout is a **safety net, not a polling interval**. The camera wakes the
loop 30–60 times a second regardless, so the loop can never sit waiting on a
client that never connects.

### The one gap poll cannot close

The loop is not always *in* `poll()`. The encoder's `QBUF` runs the job
synchronously inside the ioctl (`vepu_service()` → `rk3576_vepu_encode()`
→ `nxsem_tickwait(&g_vepu_done, ...)` at `rk3576_vepu.c:1631`), which is 24 ms on
1296x960 during which no socket is serviced. Closing that window is step (b).

## Phase 0 — baseline

Capture `us/frame:` and the frame rate for the modes in use before touching
anything. Phase A claims to change no behaviour, and that claim needs a
before-picture to be checkable against.

## Phase A — non-blocking for everything that is already an fd

| Step | Change | Behaviour change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A0 | Return the camera buffer right after the encoder's output DQBUF, instead of at the end of the frame | **yes** — shortens the grab from ~30 ms to ~24 ms |
| A1 | Open `camfd` with `O_NONBLOCK`; replace the blocking DQBUF with poll-then-dequeue, handling the `EAGAIN` race | no |
| A2 | Give `camenc_ws` an fd-collection API so the main loop can put its listen and client fds into the *same* `pollfd` array, plus a call that services only the ready ones | no |
| A3 | Make the loop an explicit state machine (`WAIT` → frame handling → `WAIT`), with the frame-in-flight state introduced now even though A's `QBUF` still blocks | no |
| A4 | A `poll()` timeout as a safety net and for periodic housekeeping | no |

**A0 is deliberately separate and separate-testable**: it changes frame timing,
so it should not be tangled with a no-behaviour-change refactor.

Expected outcome of A: connections, UI commands and mode-switch requests are
prompt (microseconds, independent of frame rate). The only remaining window is
the encode.

## Phase B — make the encode wait a poll point

**This is bigger than it first appeared, and it reverses a documented decision.**
`rk3576_vepu_codec.c:24-34` says, in the file header:

> A job is encoded synchronously, inside the ioctl that queued it. Nothing needs
> a work queue: rk3576_vepu_encode() already waits for the hardware's interrupt,
> and the framework calls output_available() from codec_qbuf(), which runs in
> task context. … simpler than handing the work to a worker and having to track
> a job across two contexts.

Making `QBUF` return early is therefore not a one-line change: the m2m framework
marks the capture buffer done in `codec_put_buf()` (`v4l2_m2m.c:1170-1177`),
which sits **inside the QBUF call chain**. Return from QBUF before the job
finishes and the framework tells the application the bitstream is ready when it
is not.

| Step | Change |
| --- | --- |
| B0 | Split `rk3576_vepu_encode()` into submit and wait, both still called synchronously from QBUF. **Semantics-preserving**, and provable: `rk3576-mpp-ref/verify_regs.py` compares the register mirror against MPP, `mutate_check.py` its mutation coverage |
| B1 | Move the completion out of the QBUF chain — the driver must signal a finished capture buffer from the completion side (a work queue, or a framework callback). This is the part the header comment argues against |
| B2 | camenc polls the encoder fd; the state machine carries a frame in flight |
| B3 | Re-measure |

### What B actually buys, and the alternative

B removes at most ~24 ms of added latency from a connection that arrives during
an encode, and turns the encode window into one where the loop can do
housekeeping. It is also the natural async boundary for a future SMP. It is
**not** a throughput win on one core.

The alternative: **leave the driver alone and give the encode its own thread**
(the main loop polls; the thread owns the encoder and signals back). Same
user-visible outcome, no driver risk, at the cost of one thread and a handoff.
Worth re-weighing now that B's real size is known — see the open questions.

has to move that tail off the caller's context, which means:

- the in-flight buffers (`cbuf`, `obuf`) and the slice state updated just after
  the wait (`gop_index`, `frame_num`, `poc_lsb`, `idr_pic_id`) must live in `priv`
  between submission and completion;
- a work queue is required for the completion, because it does cache maintenance
  and buffer bookkeeping and so cannot run in the interrupt handler;
- error reporting moves: today a failed job surfaces in the `QBUF` return value,
  and asynchronously it has to surface later, as an event or on `DQBUF`.

That is the whole of it, and it is smaller than it first looked.

| Step | Change |
| --- | --- |
| B0 | Split `rk3576_vepu_encode()` into submit and wait, both still called synchronously from QBUF. **Semantics-preserving**, and provable: `rk3576-mpp-ref/verify_regs.py` compares the register mirror against MPP, `mutate_check.py` its mutation coverage |
| B1 | Carry the job in `priv` and do the tail (`codec_output_put_buf`, the EOS event, `codec_capture_put_buf`) from a work queue on completion, so `QBUF` can return as soon as the hardware has started |
| B2 | camenc polls the encoder fd; the state machine carries a frame in flight |
| B3 | Re-measure |

### What B actually buys, and the alternative

B removes at most ~24 ms of added latency from a connection that arrives during
an encode, and turns the encode window into one where the loop can do
housekeeping. It is also the natural async boundary for a future SMP. It is
**not** a throughput win on one core.

The alternative: **leave the driver alone and give the encode its own thread**
(the main loop polls; the thread owns the encoder and signals back). The point
of that thread is not to move CPU work — a sleeping thread costs no CPU — but to
move the *wait* off the main loop. Same user-visible outcome, no driver risk, at
the cost of one thread and a handoff.

Decision (2026-10-05): **do phase A only, measure the residual latency, then
decide between B and the thread.** Both were judged to buy the same thing.

不是 CPU。而且查证之后**我上一轮的说法有错，需要更正**。

## 先回答：编码路径里没有高 CPU 环节

- **job 本身是硬件跑的**。那 24ms 是 `nxsem_tickwait(&g_vepu_done, ...)` 的**等待**，CPU 消耗接近 0。
- job 之后的收尾里唯一有点 CPU 的是对目标缓冲的 **cache invalidate**（约 1.9MB 的行遍历）+ 几个指针操作，**亚毫秒到 1ms 级**。
- 真正吃 CPU 的是 **demosaic（15ms，内核 worker）和拷贝**——都不在编码路径上。

所以"因为编码环节 CPU 高所以要开线程"这个前提不成立。**线程方案的收益从来不是把 CPU 活分出去。**

## 更正：B 比我说的小

我上一轮说"框架在 QBUF 链里标记完成，所以异步会让应用拿到半成品帧"。**这个说法不准确。** 事实是：

```c
int codec_capture_put_buf(FAR void *cookie, FAR struct v4l2_buffer *buf)  /* 公开 API */
```

它是**驱动自己调**的——`rk3576_vepu_codec.c:826`，在 `vepu_service()` 的末尾：

```
629   codec_capture_get_buf()     取目标缓冲
642   codec_output_get_buf()      取源缓冲
697   rk3576_vepu_encode()        ← 跑 job 并等待（那 24ms）
787   codec_output_put_buf()      交还源容器
826   codec_capture_put_buf()     ★ 这一帧对外"完成"的时刻
```

**"这一帧编完了"这个时刻本来就在驱动手里**，只是它现在顺手同步做掉了。**不需要动框架。**

## B 的真正困境只有一个：跨上下文

现在 `submit → 跑完 → 交还缓冲` 是一条直线，全在调用者上下文里。异步之后要拆成两半：

| | 上下文 |
|---|---|
| 提交 job（写寄存器、启动硬件） | 调用者（`QBUF`） |
| 完成收尾（invalidate cache、`put_buf`、EOS 事件） | **工作队列**（不能在 ISR 里做） |

于是必须把在飞状态从栈上搬到 `priv`：
- 在飞的 `cbuf` / `obuf`
- 紧跟 wait 之后更新的那串切片状态（`gop_index`、`frame_num`、`poc_lsb`、`idr_pic_id`）
- 以及**错误上报路径**：现在失败从 `QBUF` 返回值出来，异步后得从事件或 `DQBUF` 出来

这就是驱动头注释里那句 *"having to track a job across two contexts"* —— 作者权衡过并选择了同步，B 就是推翻这个选择。

## 那"编码线程"到底解决什么？

**它解决的不是 CPU，是等待。** 一句话：

> **睡眠不耗 CPU，但它占住了主循环。**

线程方案把那个 `nxsem_tickwait` 挪到别的线程，主循环就能 poll。所以三个选项的**收益完全一样**（≤24ms 的连接延迟 + 一个 poll 点），差别只在代价：

| 方案 | 代价 |
|---|---|
| B（驱动异步） | 跨上下文重构驱动；应用侧彻底没有等待，架构最干净 |
| 编码线程 | 驱动零改动；多一个线程和一次交接 |
| 都不做 | 最多 24ms 额外延迟 |

已经按你的决定把 memory 更正并记录了（**先只做 A，实测残留延迟后再定 B 还是线程**）——[camenc-event-loop-plan.md](.dsh/memory/camenc-event-loop-plan.md) 里那段错误描述也改掉了。

有一点值得你知道：**B 现在看比我原先讲的便宜**（不用动框架）。但它的收益没变，所以"先做 A 再实测"这个门槛依然是对的做法——测出来那 24ms 无感，就省下一次驱动重构。

text: 意思是vepu主动sleep导致不可接入poll？改造vepu驱动使之可poll，如何？

这里要把两件事分开——**驱动已经是可 poll 的**，缺的不是 poll 能力。

## 驱动今天就可 poll

```c
codec_capture_put_buf(priv->cookie, cbuf);   /* rk3576_vepu_codec.c:826 */
   └→ codec_put_buf()                        /* v4l2_m2m.c:1160 */
        ├→ video_framebuff_capture_done()
        └→ poll_notify(&cfile->fds, 1, POLLIN)   /* :1175 */
```

而且 `codec_poll` 已经注册在 `g_codec_fops` 里（`v4l2_m2m.c:218`）。所以**在编码器 fd 上 `poll()` 是能用的**，`POLLIN` 也确实会被 fire。

## 真正的问题是：驱动在**应用的线程里**睡觉

关键在于 `nxsem_tickwait(&g_vepu_done, ...)` 这一句是谁在执行：

```
camenc 线程 ──ioctl(VIDIOC_QBUF)──▶ 内核：vepu_service()
                                      └→ rk3576_vepu_encode()
                                           └→ nxsem_tickwait(...)   ← 睡的是 camenc 自己的线程
                                    ◀── 24ms 后返回
```

ioctl 是同步调用，**驱动跑的时候就是调用者的线程**。所以那 24ms 不是"驱动在别处睡"，而是"驱动把 camenc 的线程扣下来睡了 24ms"。

由此推出一个很说明问题的结论：**今天那个 `poll_notify(POLLIN)` 其实一直在 fire**——只是它 fire 的时候，应用还卡在 ioctl 里面，没人在 poll，这颗通知是**空放**的。

## 所以"改造驱动使之可 poll" 就是 B

你说的这件事，本质就是 B。但要精确表述：**不是"让驱动可 poll"（已经可 poll），而是"让驱动别在应用的线程里等"**。

要做的事只有一件：**把 `codec_capture_put_buf()` 及其前面的收尾，从现在的位置挪到 ioctl 返回之后**。

```
现在:   QBUF ─[写寄存器 → 跑 job → 睡24ms → 收尾 → put_buf → poll_notify(空放)]─ 返回
改后:   QBUF ─[写寄存器 → 启动硬件]─ 立刻返回
                              ⋮
        应用在 poll() 里睡着 ──▶ 硬件完成 → ISR → 工作队列 → 收尾 + put_buf
                                                    └→ poll_notify(POLLIN) ← 这次有人听
```

**注意"之后"这两个字的分量**：ioctl 一旦返回，收尾就没有调用者上下文可用了，必须落到另一个上下文（工作队列）。这就是全部代价所在——不是在"可 poll"上，而是在**把等待和收尾搬家并跨上下文追踪**上。

## 这对计划意味着什么

- **管道不用动**：`poll_notify` / `codec_poll` / 缓冲链表都是现成的，B 不需要碰框架。
- **要动的**：`rk3576_vepu_encode()` 拆成 submit/wait；在飞状态（`cbuf`/`obuf` + `gop_index`/`frame_num`/`poc_lsb`/`idr_pic_id`）搬进 `priv`；加一个工作队列做收尾；错误上报从 `QBUF` 返回值改道。
- **收益不变**：仍然是 ≤24ms 的连接延迟 + 编码期间多一个 poll 点。**不是吞吐收益。**

所以你的直觉——"改成可 poll 就好了"——方向对，只是**便宜的部分（可 poll）已经免费拿到了，贵的部分是把等待搬走**。

计划我不动：仍是**先做 A、实测残留延迟、再定 B 还是线程**。如果你的意思是现在就上 B，说一声我就把顺序调过来；另外 **B0（submit/wait 拆分，语义不变）可以随时单独做**——它不改变任何行为，还能用 `verify_regs.py` / `mutate_check.py` 证明无副作用，是给 B 铺路的最安全一步。

要现在开始吗？我建议先从 **A0** 动手（相机缓冲提前归还），它独立、便宜、直接关系帧率，且不等任何讨论。

text:
我这样理解对不对：
原先，获得容器，等待vepu，归还容器，这三个事情是合在一次调用里的
B方案则是把它们拆开，由状态机来管理容器的获得与归还（而不是由等待的那次调用）

前半句对，**后半句有一处要修正**，而且这处修正很重要——它决定了应用侧要写多少代码。

## 对的部分

`vepu_service()` 里确实是三件事串在一次调用里，而这次调用来自 `QBUF` ioctl：

```
629   cbuf = codec_capture_get_buf(cookie)     获得目标容器
642   obuf = codec_output_get_buf(cookie)      获得源容器
697   rk3576_vepu_encode(...)                  启动 + 等 VEPU（那 24ms）
787   codec_output_put_buf(cookie, obuf)       归还源容器
826   codec_capture_put_buf(cookie, cbuf)      归还目标容器
```

## 要修正的部分：容器管理**不能**交给应用的状态机

`codec_capture_get_buf()` / `codec_capture_put_buf()` 是**驱动内部 API**（内核侧，参数是 `void *cookie` 这种 `codec_file_t` 指针），应用根本够不着——应用对编码器的全部接口仍然只有 `QBUF` / `DQBUF`。

所以容器仍然是驱动在管。B 改的**不是"谁管"，而是"在哪里、什么时候管"**：

```
现在 —— 一次调用内全部完成：
  QBUF ioctl:
    get(cbuf) → get(obuf) → [启动硬件 · 睡24ms · 收尾] → put(obuf) → put(cbuf)
  应用回来时：容器已归还，码流已可 DQBUF

B 之后：
  QBUF ioctl:
    get(cbuf) → get(obuf) → 启动硬件 → 立刻返回      ← 容器还欠着，记在 priv 里
  应用: poll(编码器 fd) 睡着
  硬件完成 → ISR → 工作队列:
    收尾 → put(obuf) → put(cbuf) → poll_notify(POLLIN) → 应用醒
  DQBUF: 取出码流
```

准确的说法是：**"获得"留在原地，"等待"被删掉，"归还"搬到完成上下文。**

## 那应用的状态机管什么？

管**它自己那一侧**的"帧在飞"，具体两件：

1. **相机缓冲的持有与归还** —— 这是应用自己的池（零拷贝下尤其关键，就是 A0 在动的那块）
2. **"已投递一帧、正在等编码器 POLLIN"** 这个状态 —— 它决定 poll 里要不要关心编码器 fd

而编码器的容器对应用始终是**不透明的**，只有 QBUF/DQBUF 两个动作，B 不改变这一点。

## 所以 B 的施工内容，用你这个框架重新表述

| 东西 | 现在在哪 | B 之后 |
|---|---|---|
| `cbuf` / `obuf` | `vepu_service()` 的**栈**上 | `priv` 里（跨上下文） |
| 切片状态 `gop_index`/`frame_num`/`poc_lsb`/`idr_pic_id` | 紧跟 wait 之后更新 | 也进 `priv`，在完成侧更新 |
| 等待 | 调用者线程里 `nxsem_tickwait` | 消失（应用改用 poll） |
| 收尾（invalidate cache、put_buf、EOS 事件） | 调用者上下文 | **工作队列** |

## 正确的框法：延迟 ≈ 主循环"离开 poll 的最长连续时长"

不做 B 时，一帧里有这么一段是**回不到 poll** 的：

```
poll 返回 → DQBUF → [拷贝] → QBUF(encode 24ms) → DQBUF → mux → 回 poll
                              └────────── 这段时间网络无人理会 ──────────┘
```

用实测数字（1296x960，记忆里的 `us/frame: camera 1617 copy 6037 mux 776` + `encode 23958`）：

| | 离开 poll 的时长 |
|---|---|
| **不做 B**（零拷贝已生效，copy=0） | encode 24.0 + mux 0.8 ≈ **24.7ms** |
| **做了 B** | mux 0.8 ≈ **0.8ms** |

约 **30 倍**的差距。而且关键一点：**这个延迟随分辨率增长**——1080p 的编码更长，窗口更大。它不是个固定的小数字。

## 但要说清它影响什么、不影响什么

**不影响视频数据面。** 码流在编码完成之前根本不存在，**B 不可能让任何一帧更早到达**。"24ms vs 33.3ms"这个比例衡量的是**流水线延迟**，不是 B 能修的东西。这一点很重要，否则容易以为 B 能让画面更流畅。

**影响的是控制面**：
- 新客户端连接 + HTTP 响应
- 已连接客户端的 UI 命令（拖滑条、切模式）
- 给落后客户端排空发送缓冲
- 接受模式切换请求

## ★ 一个我该早点说的点：不做 B，也**达不到"纯非阻塞"**

encode 是当前最大的窗口，但**不是唯一的**。同一帧里 mux / file / clients 那段尾巴一样把网络挡在外面。而历史数据里这些尾巴会尖峰：

```
mux 峰值 2041µs   file 峰值 1813µs   camera 峰值 66597µs（66.6ms）
```

如果 file 写盘卡住 200ms，网络就死 200ms——**这个 B 修不了**。要真正做到"任何时候都能及时响应"，emit 那一侧也得变成"入队"（有界段队列 + sink 线程/或至少不阻塞的写）。

所以准确的说法是：

> **B 把最大的一个窗口（encode）从 24.7ms 降到 0.8ms；剩下的窗口靠 sink 队列解决。**

我上一轮说"B 的收益只有 ≤24ms，值不值得存疑"。**这个说法不准确**，应该是：

- B 的收益是**把一个随分辨率增长的 ~25ms 控制面延迟降到 ms 级**，约 30 倍
- 代价是一次跨上下文的驱动重构（不用动框架，B0 还能用寄存器 harness 证明语义不变）
- 收益仍**不包含吞吐**——单核上帧率不会变

这个交易比我之前讲的**明显更值得**。

但我还是建议**先量一次再拍板**，理由是量的成本几乎为零——A 做完后，`us/frame` 里 `sum − camera` 就是"离开 poll 的时长"，直接读出来。如果实测是 25ms 量级，那 B 就该做；如果发现尾巴的尖峰（mux/file）其实比 encode 更常挡路，那**先做 sink 队列**比 B 更划算。

## 需要你定的

1. **按原计划**：先 A0 → A → 实测 `sum − camera` → 再定 B 还是 sink
2. **顺序调过来**：先做 B0（submit/wait 拆分，语义不变、可用 harness 证明）——它不改变行为，随时可做，也是给 B 铺路的最安全一步；然后再走 A

我倾向 1，但如果你觉得 25ms 已经不能接受，2 也成立——只是**上板验证的次数会多一次**。

另外补一句：**sink 队列这件事，B 和 threading 都替代不了**。它不依赖 B 的结论，可以独立排期。要不要我把它也列进 memory 的计划里，作为一个独立条目？

Decision (2026-10-05): **phase B is committed, and is not gated on a
measurement.**

The reason is not performance. The current version's performance is already
sufficient. The conversion is being done for **software-engineering quality**:
this is a code sample delivered to other engineers, so the cost of
understanding it is part of what is being delivered. A loop that is
non-blocking everywhere except one 24 ms hole in the middle is not a smaller
thing to read than one that never blocks — it is a larger thing, because the
exception has to be found, understood and remembered. B removes the exception.

That reframing supersedes the earlier "measure first, then decide": the
measurement would only have settled whether the residual latency mattered,
and it does not matter. What matters is that there is no residual.

It also sets the priority for every choice inside the work: **prefer the
arrangement a reader gets right the first time over the one that is marginally
faster.**

### Construction order

| Order | Step | Board needed | Why here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A0 — return the camera buffer as soon as the loop is done with it | yes (frame timing changes) | independent, small, and it changes timing, so it must not share a flash with a no-behaviour-change refactor |
| 2 | A1–A4 — the loop becomes `poll`-driven, non-blocking DQBUF, `camenc_ws` fds in the same set | yes (regression only) | claims to change no behaviour; verified by comparison |
| 3 | B0 — split `rk3576_vepu_encode()` into submit and wait, still called synchronously | **no** | semantics-preserving, provable offline with the register harnesses |
| 4 | B1 + B2 — completion moves to a work queue; camenc polls the encoder fd | yes | the two must land together: the driver without the poller leaves the loop blocking in `DQBUF` instead |

### Not covered by B

The emit tail — mux, the file write, the client fan-out — is *also* an
interval during which the loop is not in `poll`. B removes the encode window
only. Measured spikes are smaller (`mux` max 2.0 ms, `file` max 1.8 ms on
640x480) but the file write has no bound at all, so a stalled filesystem still
blocks the network.

Making that side non-blocking too means handing segments to a bounded queue and
letting a sink thread drain it. That is an independent item, not a dependency
of B, and it is **not** in this plan; recorded in `camenc-refactor-state.md`
as the one place a thread has a real payoff.

**A `-n` frame count is not a duration**: `-n 100` is three seconds of runtime,
after which the program exits and the port closes. Worth remembering when a
browser "times out" — nothing is listening by then.

### A1–A4 — implemented, awaiting the board

The loop now sleeps in exactly one place, and it sleeps on everything at once.

| Step | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| A1 | `camfd` is opened `O_NONBLOCK`; a dequeue with nothing ready answers `EAGAIN`, which `camenc_dequeue()` returns without reporting and the loop reads as "not yet" rather than as a fault |
| A2 | `camenc_ws_poll()` is gone. The server now offers its sockets through `camenc_ws_fds()` and acts on the ready ones through `camenc_ws_ready()`, so the camera and the network are waited on by one `poll()` |
| A3 | The loop is `for (; i < frames; )` with `i++` at the end of the body: a round that served the server and found no frame has not used a frame number and returns to the same one |
| A4 | The wait is bounded by `CAMENC_WAIT_MS` (500 ms) as a safety net for a board where the camera has stopped too — **not** as a polling interval; the camera wakes it 30–60 times a second regardless |

`camenc_wait()` is the whole of it: it fills the array, polls, accounts the wait
as the `camera` stage and the service as the `serve` stage, and reports whether
the camera has a frame. A source that is not the camera is never waited for —
its wait has a zero timeout and only serves the sockets.

Two consequences worth remembering:

- **`camera` in the `us/frame` line still means "time spent waiting"**, which is
  what it always measured; the dequeue after it no longer waits, so the figure
  stays comparable with earlier runs.
- **The `serve` stage now measures the same work as before**, but it happens
  when a socket is ready rather than once per frame, so it should be smaller —
  and a client that connects during the *inter-frame* wait is answered within
  that wait instead of at the end of the frame. The encode window is still not
  reachable; that is B.

`camenc_ws_ready()` reads a client for `POLLIN | POLLHUP | POLLERR` and flushes
it only for `POLLOUT`, which `camenc_ws_fds()` asks for only when something is
queued for that client — a writable socket with nothing to write would wake the
loop for nothing.

### Git state

`-z` was removed and is gone from source and firmware. The A0 change is
**staged** (30 insertions, 10 deletions on `camenc_main.c`); A1–A4 are unstaged
on top of it, so the two can be committed separately — which is what the

camenc: wait for the frame and the network together

The capture loop waited in VIDIOC_DQBUF, and that call covers one thing.  A
client connecting, a slider being dragged or a mode being chosen all waited
for whichever frame was in progress to finish before anything noticed them;
and the wait itself, which is the longest stretch the loop spends with
nothing to do, was spent unable to hear the network at all.  camenc_ws_poll()
then ran once per frame whether or not it had anything to do.

The loop now waits in poll() on the camera and on every socket the server
owns, so it is woken by whichever of them happens first.  That is the whole
of the arrangement: a waiting poll costs no CPU, it is answered as soon as
any source is ready, and the camera is what usually answers it, so the loop
sleeps as deeply as it did and hears everything.

  - camfd is opened non-blocking.  A dequeue with nothing ready answers
    EAGAIN, which camenc_dequeue() returns without reporting and the loop
    reads as "not yet" rather than as a fault.
  - The server no longer waits and is no longer polled.  It offers its
    descriptors through camenc_ws_fds() and acts on the ready ones through
    camenc_ws_ready(), so one wait covers the camera and every client.
  - The frame number is advanced by the loop's body rather than by the loop,
    because a round that served the server and found no frame has not used
    one and must come back to the same number.
  - Writability is asked for only when there is something queued for that
    client.  A socket that is writable with nothing to write would wake the
    loop for nothing, once per frame.
  - The wait has a bound, and it is a bound and not a polling interval.  It
    will not normally expire: the camera answers thirty to sixty times a
    second whatever it says.  It is there so that a board whose camera has
    stopped as well still comes back round.

The camera's buffer is now returned as soon as the loop has finished reading
it, which is once the encoder has handed its input container back, rather
than at the end of the frame.  Where the frame is encoded where it lies that
buffer *is* the encoder's source, so the capture driver could not write
another frame into it for most of a frame period and was a buffer short for
all of it.  Measured at 1280x720: no overruns, nothing dropped for want of a
buffer, no races.

What this does not change is the encode.  It still runs inside the queue
operation, so the loop is still away from the wait for its duration -- about
24 ms at 1296x960 -- and a connection that arrives inside that window still
waits for it.  Removing that one is a change to the encoder driver and is
not this one.

### B0 — implemented, verified by the boot selftest

`rk3576_vepu_encode()` is now a wrapper over two halves:

| Function | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `vepu_start_locked()` | everything up to the write that starts the hardware |
| `vepu_wait_locked()` | the wait, the status, the slice FIFO, the reconstruction slot |
| `rk3576_vepu_encode()` | validations → take `g_vepu_lock` → start → wait → drop the reference on failure → unlock |

Two things about the shape, both found by reading rather than assumed:

- **`g_vepu_lock` is held across the whole encode**, so it cannot be released
  between the halves — the hardware runs one job at a time and the lock is what
  says whose it is. In B1 the completion is therefore what releases it.
- **The halves share no state.** The working copy of the frame (`job`), the
  register base and the start command are all start-side; the interrupt status,
  the two lengths and the FIFO's completion flag are all wait-side. `frm`,
  `slice` and `result` are the only things that cross, and they are all
  arguments. So the split is a cut, not a redesign.

Every `goto errout_unlock` became `return ret`, and the label's two jobs — drop
the reference on failure, unlock — moved into the wrapper, in that order.

★ **The plan's verification claim for B0 was wrong.** `verify_regs.py` and
`mutate_check.py` cover the *register layer*; B0 changes no register write, only
control flow, so neither harness can see it. What does cover it is
`CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST`, which is **enabled in this config** and runs
`rk3576_vepu_selftest()` at every boot from `kickpi_k7_boardinit.c:640`,
logging `ERROR: rk3576_vepu_selftest failed: N` if it fails. B0 is therefore
verified by booting the board.

### What B1 has to do, now that the split exists

`rk3576_vepu_codec.c` currently calls the encoder synchronously from
`vepu_service()`, which runs inside the `QBUF` ioctl, and does its own tail
inline: `codec_output_put_buf()`, the EOS event, `codec_capture_put_buf()`.
B1 is:

- call `vepu_start_locked()`-equivalent from `QBUF` and return, remembering the
  in-flight `cbuf`/`obuf` and the slice state that is updated just after the
  wait (`gop_index`, `frame_num`, `poc_lsb`, `idr_pic_id`) in `priv`;
- run the wait and the tail from a **work queue** on completion — not from the
  interrupt handler, which cannot do cache maintenance or touch the buffer
  lists;
- release `g_vepu_lock` there, and report a failure as an event or on `DQBUF`
  rather than through the `QBUF` return value.

## 读出来的两件事（计划里没写对）

**1. `g_vepu_lock` 是跨整个 encode 持有的**，所以**不能**在两半之间释放——硬件同时只跑一个 job，锁就是"这个 job 归谁"的凭据。⇒ **B1 里释放锁的必须是完成侧**，这个约束现在明确了。

| 只属于 start | 只属于 wait | 跨两半 |
|---|---|---|
| `base`、`job`、`start` | `intsta`、`status_length`、`bs_length`、`complete` | 只有参数 `frm` / `slice` / `result` |

所以这是一次**干净的切断**，不是重新设计。所有 `goto errout_unlock` 改成 `return ret`，标签原来的两件工作（失败丢参考、解锁）按原顺序移进 wrapper。

```c

  int ret = rk3576_vepu_selftest();          /* 每次启动都跑 */
  if (ret < 0) syslog(LOG_ERR, "ERROR: rk3576_vepu_selftest failed: %d\n", ret);
#endif
```

⇒ **B0 由"开机"本身验证**：下一次烧录启动时，串口没有 `rk3576_vepu_selftest failed` 就说明拆分没有改变行为。不需要额外测试。

`rk3576_vepu_codec.c` 现在把三件事全塞在 `vepu_service()` 里、由 `QBUF` ioctl 同步跑。B1 是：

1. `QBUF` 里只**启动**，把在飞的 `cbuf`/`obuf` 和紧跟在等待之后更新的切片状态（`gop_index`/`frame_num`/`poc_lsb`/`idr_pic_id`）记进 `priv`，然后返回；

input.prompt:
You are working in a NuttX-based openvela workspace at `/home/yunline/projects/ovela-dev-workspace`. Implement a kernel-driver change known as "B1". Read this brief fully before touching anything. Work only in this repo; do not commit (leave changes unstaged).

## Context

`contest2026_062_PharosTech` is the code repository. `chips/` and `boards/` are symlinks into `vendor/rockchip/`, so editing either path edits the same file the build reads.

The VEPU510 is a hardware H.264 encoder. Its V4L2 driver is
`chips/rk3576/vepu/rk3576_vepu_codec.c` (device plumbing, ~1700 lines), which sits on top of the register/sequence driver `chips/rk3576/vepu/rk3576_vepu.c` (hardware, ~2800 lines).

**Today the encode is synchronous.** The application's `VIDIOC_QBUF` on the encoder's OUTPUT queue runs the whole job inside the ioctl: the driver takes a capture container and the output container, builds the frame, calls `rk3576_vepu_encode(...)` which starts the hardware and waits for the interrupt, then does the post-job work inline and returns. The application then dequeues the bitstream.

The problem being fixed: `QBUF` blocking for the whole encode (~24 ms) means the application's single-threaded event loop cannot service its network sockets during it.

**A prerequisite change (call it B0) is already done and verified on hardware.** `rk3576_vepu_encode()` in `rk3576_vepu.c` is now a wrapper over two static helpers:
- `vepu_start_locked(frm, cfg, slice)` — everything up to and including the register write that starts the hardware. Returns `OK` with the job running.
- `vepu_wait_locked(frm, slice, result)` — waits for the interrupt, reads status, drains the slice FIFO, advances the reconstruction slot.
The wrapper `rk3576_vepu_encode()` does: validate args (returns `-EINVAL` before locking) → `nxmutex_lock(&g_vepu_lock)` → `vepu_start_locked()` → if that succeeded, `vepu_wait_locked()` → if the result is negative, set `g_vepu_recn_ref_valid = false` → `nxmutex_unlock(&g_vepu_lock)` → return.

**Critical invariant:** `g_vepu_lock` is taken and released across the whole encode and MUST NOT be released between the two halves. The hardware runs one job at a time and the lock is what says whose it is.

## What to implement

### Part A — expose the two halves in `rk3576_vepu.c` / `rk3576_vepu.h`

Add two public functions and re-express `rk3576_vepu_encode()` in terms of them:

- `int rk3576_vepu_start(frm, cfg, slice)` — validate, take `g_vepu_lock`, call `vepu_start_locked()`. On failure: set `g_vepu_recn_ref_valid = false`, release the lock, return the error. On success: return `OK` **with the lock still held**.
- `int rk3576_vepu_finish(frm, slice, result)` — call `vepu_wait_locked()`, set `g_vepu_recn_ref_valid = false` on failure, release the lock, return.
- `rk3576_vepu_encode()` = validate → `rk3576_vepu_start()` → if OK, `rk3576_vepu_finish()`.

**The observable behaviour of `rk3576_vepu_encode()` must not change at all.** The boot self-test calls it directly (see Verification) and covers it. Document in `rk3576_vepu.h` that the lock is held between a successful start and its finish, and why (one job at a time).

### Part B — make the codec driver asynchronous

In `rk3576_vepu_codec.c`, `vepu_service()` (starts at line ~601) must stop waiting. Restructure:

1. `vepu_service()` starts the job and returns immediately after the hardware has been given it. The post-job work must NOT run there.
2. The wait and the post-job work move to a **work queue** item, which runs when the interrupt has been taken.
3. The in-flight state must live in `priv` (`struct rk3576_vepu_codec_priv_s`) between the two: the capture container and the output container that were taken, plus anything the post-job half needs. Note `priv` already holds the slice state (`gop_index`, `frame_num`, `poc_lsb`, `idr_pic_id`, `frame_index`) and `output_pending` / `eos_pending`.
4. The post-job half must do exactly what `vepu_service()` does today after the encoder returns:
   - `priv->gop_index++` and wrap, `frame_num` / `poc_lsb` advance, `priv->frame_index++`, `priv->output_pending = false`
   - `codec_output_put_buf(priv->cookie, obuf)`
   - the EOS handling: flag the capture buffer `V4L2_BUF_FLAG_LAST`, set `bytesused = 0` if nothing was encoded, clear `eos_pending`, and queue the `V4L2_EVENT_EOS` event via `codec_queue_event()`
   - `codec_capture_put_buf(priv->cookie, cbuf)` — **this is what publishes the frame to the application**; the m2m framework's `poll_notify(POLLIN)` happens inside it, which is what will later wake the application's `poll()`. It must still be called exactly once per finished job, and must not be called until the job is genuinely finished.

## Constraints you must respect

- **One job at a time.** If a job is already in flight, `vepu_service()` must not start a second one. Leave the frame pending and return `OK` — this matches how the function already handles a full capture queue ("back pressure rather than a lost frame"). Do not return an error.
- **The interrupt handler cannot do this work.** The post-job half does cache maintenance (`up_invalidate_dcache` over the destination) and touches framework buffer lists, so it must run in task context, i.e. the work queue.
- **Choose the work queue deliberately and say why in a comment.** `LPWORK` is priority 100 and shared with, among others, the camera capture driver's 15 ms demosaic job; `HPWORK` is priority 192. The completion is short (one cache invalidation over roughly the bitstream buffer) but the next frame cannot start until it has run. Make a reasoned choice and document the tradeoff in a comment. Do not silently pick one.
- **Error reporting changes shape.** Today a failed job surfaces as a negative return from the `QBUF` ioctl. Asynchronously it has to surface later. Handle it sensibly: at minimum log it, and do not publish a buffer as a valid frame when the job failed. If you find an existing event mechanism that fits, use it; explain what you chose and what a caller can and cannot learn. Note the application currently relies on `QBUF` failures being visible, so think about what happens to it.
- **Update the stale file-header comment.** `rk3576_vepu_codec.c` lines ~24-34 currently explain that "A job is encoded synchronously, inside the ioctl that queued it. Nothing needs a work queue...". That is no longer true. Rewrite it to describe the new arrangement and why it changed.
- **The application must keep working without changes.** `camenc` currently does: QBUF the input, DQBUF the input container (drain), DQBUF the bitstream, mux, QBUF both back. With an asynchronous driver its QBUF returns early and its first DQBUF blocks until the job finishes — which is correct, just blocked slightly later. Confirm you have not broken that ordering.

## Style — this matters as much as the code

This is a code sample delivered to other engineers, so comprehension cost is a first-class requirement. Match the surrounding code exactly:
- Comments are long explanatory prose that say **why**, not what. Look at any neighbouring comment before writing one. They are written in complete sentences, use `--` for a dash, and avoid lists in code comments.
- `clang-format` owns formatting: run `clang-format -i <file>` from the repository root (there is a `.clang-format` there) and do not hand-wrap to 79 columns. Note clang-format is version 14.
- No dead code, no unused parameters, no "just in case" fields. The build uses `-Wall -Werror`.
- Keep the change minimal and local. Do not refactor anything you were not asked to.

## Build and verify

```sh
cd /home/yunline/projects/ovela-dev-workspace
export PATH="$PWD/prebuilts/gcc/linux-x86_64/aarch64-none-elf/bin:$PATH"
export CCACHE_DISABLE=1
prebuilts/tools/ninja/bin/ninja -C cmake_out/contest2026_062_PharosTech_camera
```

Must end with exit code 0 and no warnings. Firmware lands at `cmake_out/contest2026_062_PharosTech_camera/nuttx.bin`.

You cannot run this on hardware. `CONFIG_RK3576_VEPU_SELFTEST` is enabled and `rk3576_vepu_selftest()` runs at every boot from `boards/rk3576/kickpi-k7/src/kickpi_k7_boardinit.c:640`; it exercises the synchronous `rk3576_vepu_encode()` path and would catch a regression there. Read its code — especially `rk3576_vepu_selftest_sequence()` — to convince yourself your Part A change keeps that path equivalent.

## Report back

When done, report concisely:
1. What you changed, file by file, with line references.
2. The exact build result.
3. Which work queue you chose and why.
4. What you are **not** confident about, and anything you could not verify without hardware. Be specific and honest — do not claim verification you did not do.
5. Any place where the code's existing comments contradict what you implemented (the repository has a history of stale comments; flag them rather than silently rewriting).

B1 已经交给子代理实现，我给它写了一份完整的交接说明。核心设计约束都在里面：

**Part A —— `rk3576_vepu.c/.h` 导出两个半段**

```
rk3576_vepu_start(frm, cfg, slice)     // 取锁、启动；成功则"带着锁"返回
rk3576_vepu_finish(frm, slice, result) // 等待、收尾；在这里释放锁
rk3576_vepu_encode() = start + finish   // 行为必须一字不变
```

锁的所有权契约写进了说明——**成功 start 到 finish 之间锁不允许释放**，这是我上一轮从代码里读出来的硬约束，不是可选的。

**Part B —— `rk3576_vepu_codec.c` 异步化**，以及几条我明确要求它遵守的：

| 约束 | 原因 |
|---|---|
| 有 job 在飞时**不再启动第二个**，让帧保持 pending 并返回 OK | 与既有的"capture 队列满即背压，而不是丢帧"一致 |
| 收尾必须走**工作队列**，不能放 ISR | 它要做 cache 维护和动框架缓冲链表 |
| **工作队列选 LPWORK 还是 HPWORK 必须论证并写进注释** | LPWORK 与 VICAP 那个 15ms 去马赛克共享；HPWORK 会抢占它。这个取舍我不替它拍板，但要求它说清 |
| **错误上报改道**：从 `QBUF` 返回值改成完成侧 | 这是异步化固有的、也是最容易被忽略的一处 |

### B1 + B2 — implemented, not yet on hardware

★ **The brief's premise about the application was wrong, and the correction
matters.** It said an asynchronous driver would leave camenc blocking in
`DQBUF`. It does not block: `codec_dqbuf()` returns `-EAGAIN` unconditionally
when the queue is empty (`nuttx/drivers/video/v4l2_m2m.c:538`), with no
semaphore and no `O_NONBLOCK` check, and nothing above it retries. So an
asynchronous driver makes camenc's two encoder dequeues fail within
microseconds, and its `if (ret < 0) break` would stop the run on the first
frame. **B1 and B2 have to land together** — which the order above already
said, but for the wrong reason.

There is a framework asymmetry behind this, worth remembering:

| Framework | `DQBUF` with nothing ready |
| --- | --- |
| `v4l2_cap` (camera) | waits, unless the fd is `O_NONBLOCK` — which is why camfd has it |
| `v4l2_m2m` (encoder) | always `-EAGAIN`; the flag changes nothing |

Invisible while the driver was synchronous, because `QBUF` returned with the
frame already done.

What was built:

- `rk3576_vepu_start()` / `rk3576_vepu_finish()` exported; `rk3576_vepu_encode()`
  is exactly start-then-finish with no gap, and validation lives only in
  `start` so there is no second copy to drift.
- `rk3576_vepu_codec.c`: `vepu_service_locked()` starts and returns;
  `vepu_job_work()` on **HPWORK** waits and finishes; `priv->lock` serialises
  the ioctl context against the worker; `vepu_job_settle()` handles
  close/streamoff racing a job in flight.
- The completion is on HPWORK because it is what releases `g_vepu_lock`; behind
  LPWORK it would queue behind the camera's ~15 ms demosaic every frame.
- `camenc_main.c`: the encoder fd joins the single `poll()`; the frame path is
  a completion half and an idle half with `inflight` carried across rounds;
  `-EAGAIN` on both encoder dequeues means "not yet".

**Behaviour changes to be aware of, all deliberate:**

1. **A failed job no longer fails `QBUF`.** There is no error event in this
   framework, so a post-start failure now publishes an empty capture buffer
   (the convention the flush marker already used) and forces an IDR. camenc
   counts that as a dropped frame and carries on, where it used to abort the
   run. A caller can detect *that* a frame was empty, not *why*.
2. **The `us/frame` stages changed meaning.** `camera` now includes the encode
   wait and `encode` is only the submission. Names kept so the line stays
   comparable with phase-A logs, which means the labels are loose.
3. `chips/rk3576/Kconfig` gained `select SCHED_WORKQUEUE` / `SCHED_HPWORK`,
   outside both briefs. The current `.config` already has both.

**Not verified: nothing has run on hardware.** In particular the codec fd's
`poll()` wake-up (`POLLIN` = bitstream ready, `POLLOUT` = input container back)
is read from the source and is now depended on by the boot codec self-test,
which waits with `poll()` bounded at 5 s — so a board that boots cleanly and
passes that self-test has also exercised it. Failure signatures to look for:
`VEPU0 codec frame N did not arrive`, or `DQBUF after frame N failed: 11`.

**Stale comments found and deliberately left alone** (fix them when the area is
next touched): `priv`'s `frame_index /* counts frames for idr_pic_id */` is
simply wrong; camenc's file header still claims a camera buffer cannot be
handed to the encoder, which the committed zero-copy path contradicts;
`vepu510_regs.c:105` should now point at `rk3576_vepu_start()`; and
`rk3576_vepu.h`'s "current scope: power domain, resets, clocks and a version
probe" has been false for a long time.

### What B1 needs from `rk3576_vepu.c` first

The codec driver has to start a job inside `QBUF` and finish it later, but
`rk3576_vepu_encode()` both takes and releases `g_vepu_lock`. So the first step
of B1 is to export the two halves with the lock's ownership made explicit:

| Export | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `rk3576_vepu_start(frm, cfg, slice)` | takes the lock, validates, starts the hardware; on failure drops the reference, releases the lock and returns the error; on success returns `OK` **with the lock held** |
| `rk3576_vepu_finish(frm, slice, result)` | waits, finishes the job, drops the reference on failure, releases the lock |

`rk3576_vepu_encode()` then becomes `start` followed by `finish`, so its own
behaviour is unchanged and the boot selftest still covers it.

健康的窗口也证明了这点：`sum 31049 vs period 31098`、32.2fps 时，服务端一切都正常。

相机每 31ms 就该来一帧。**唯一能让它 200ms 不来的原因是 VICAP 没有空闲缓冲可写。**

而 B2 里相机缓冲是在**完成半段、收到 `POLLOUT` 时**归还的：

> "the camera buffer is still returned the moment the input container comes back"

也就是说：

```
编码器 output 容器被归还 (POLLOUT 触发)
        ↓
相机缓冲才归还 → VICAP 才能写下一帧 → camfd 才可读 → poll 才返回
```

**这条链断一节，相机就饿死，poll 就干等，帧率就崩——而 WS 只是最先被看见的受害者。**

关掉了，编译通过。

## 做法

在**两个 VEPU 驱动文件**里（`rk3576_vepu.c`、`rk3576_vepu_codec.c`）把 `_info` 和 `_warn` 改成 `_none`——**就是 `debug.h` 在对应级别关掉时用的同一套写法**（`#undef` + `#define _info _none`），所以行为和"配置关掉"完全一致，不引入新语义。

每处都是一整块、带注释、标明"Remove this block to bring the driver's lines back"，删掉即恢复。

## 我故意没做的两件事

**1. 没有用 `CONFIG_DEBUG_*` 去改 defconfig。** 那是一刀切：`_err/_warn/_info` 是 `debug.h` 里的全局宏，关掉会**连 `CAMENC WS:` 那批行一起灭掉**——而 `ws_accept` / `ws_serve_upgrade` / `client went away` 正是查 WS 问题唯一的证据。所以只在 VEPU 这两个文件里局部关。

**2. 没有关 `_err`。** 它不会逐帧重复，所以不是干扰源；而它是驱动报告真实故障的唯一出口（比如自检失败）。要一起关的话再加两行就行。

## 一点提醒：交错不会完全消失

交错其实来自**两条不同的输出通道**：

| 来源 | 通道 |
|---|---|
| VEPU 驱动（现已静音） | syslog |
| **`camenc_ws.c` 的 `CAMENC WS:` 行** | **syslog** |
| `camenc_main.c` 的 `us/frame` / `frame NNN` / `3a` | **stdout** |

所以静音 VEPU 之后，**`CAMENC WS:` 那批行仍会和主循环的 `printf` 交错**。它们现在是你查 WS 问题要用的，所以我留着；等你不需要了，说一声我用同样的方式把 `camenc_ws.c` 也静音——那时主循环的日志就是干净的。

## 我在 NuttX 里查到的（已核实）

这正是我上一步改造动过的地方：**flush 从"每帧无条件"变成了"只在 POLLOUT 时"**。而 NuttX 的 TCP poll 唤醒路径有缺口：

```c
if ((flags & (TCP_NEWDATA | TCP_BACKLOG | TCP_RXCLOSE)) != 0)  eventset |= POLLIN;
if ((flags & TCP_CONNECTED) != 0)                              eventset |= POLLOUT;
if ((flags & TCP_DISCONN_EVENTS) != 0)                         /* 断开 */
```

**只有 `TCP_CONNECTED`（建连瞬间那一次）会产生 POLLOUT，`TCP_POLL` 没有任何映射。**

1. 客户端第一次发不完自己的数据（大 IDR 撞上慢速链路），`tx` 积压；
2. 之后服务器再也不为这条 socket 醒来 → 不再 flush；

**不要只靠 POLLOUT 触发 flush。** 恢复"每轮都试着 flush 有积压的客户端"，把 POLLOUT 当成加速器而不是唯一扳机——这正是改造前 `camenc_ws_poll()` 的行为。`ws_flush()` 在 `tx_len == tx_sent` 时会立刻返回，所以对已经排空的客户端几乎没有代价。

`rk3576_vepu.h`'s "current scope: power domain, resets, clocks and a version
probe" has been false for a long time.

## ★ The open defect: a connection left unserved for ~100 seconds

Seen with the committed build, and **not** fixed. It predates the event-loop
work — a stall has been seen before — but the work makes it easier to reach.

**Wireshark, one occurrence:** the client's SYN at t=77 s, the server's first
PSH at t=174 s. **97 seconds.** The server's receive window stayed at 65535 and
it sent *nothing* — so this is not a socket or buffer problem, the application
simply never wrote.

**The arithmetic matters more than the duration.** 97 s is about 2900 frames at
30/s, and the frame counter kept advancing throughout: the loop was alive and
returning to its `poll()`. So this is a **servicing failure** — the connection
sat unaccepted or unread — and not a frozen loop. Anything that explains it must
also explain why the loop kept running.

The symptoms that travel with it, in the order they were found:

1. `us/frame` shows the `camera` stage at 200–700 ms and the rate collapsing to
   2.5 fps, then recovering. `camera` is now the `poll()` wait, so a long one
   means nothing in the set became ready.
2. `ws_warn_full: a 13080-byte frame does not fit 520253 of 528400 bytes` — a
   client's transmit buffer at 98.5%. The parameter order is `len`, `tx_len`,
   `tx_size`, so this is *not* a buffer that is too small; the socket was not
   draining. But the capture above shows the window open, so the buffer filling
   is a **consequence** of the application not flushing, not a cause.

**A NuttX gap found on the way, and probably relevant.** In
`nuttx/net/tcp/tcp_netpoll.c`, registering interest in `POLLOUT` does set
`cb->flags |= TCP_POLL` (`:271`), but the poll callback never maps `TCP_POLL`
back to `POLLOUT` — the only `POLLOUT` it produces is from `TCP_CONNECTED`
(`:95`), which happens once, at connection setup. So a task already blocked in
`poll()` is **not woken by a socket's send buffer draining**, even though it
asked to be. Whether a *fresh* `poll()` call still reports `POLLOUT` from
current state was not checked, and that decides whether the fix is simply to
flush opportunistically instead of relying on the event.

**The next experiment is cheap and separates the two remaining hypotheses.** Add
a counter to `camenc_wait()` and one to `ws_accept()`, then reproduce a refresh:

| Observation | Reading |
| --- | --- |
| `camenc_wait()` called thousands of times a second instead of ~30 | the loop is **spinning** — most likely `encfd` reporting `POLLOUT` continuously while a frame is in flight, which would also starve the camera's LPWORK worker and explain the 200–700 ms `camera` stage |
| rounds climbing while `ws_accept()` does not | the listening socket's `POLLIN` is never delivered, so the connection waits in the backlog |

The spin hypothesis is the one that explains the most: it accounts for the frame
rate collapse, for the connection not being served, for appearing only after
B1/B2, and for needing a client to be connected at all (with none, there is no
`POLLOUT` to ask about).

Two other things to carry forward: `CAMENC_WAIT_FDS` was one short and is fixed
in `5249993` (it is now `CAMENC_WS_MAX_CLIENTS + 2` — one for the camera or the
encoder, one for the listening socket, one per client); and Firefox's HTTP
connection timeout is about 90 s, which is uncomfortably close to the 97 s
observed, so the page probably appeared only because the server recovered just
before the client gave up.
